- [USER] User expressed interest in the Spartan training regimen and its duration.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Spartan training regimen began at the age of 7 and lasted until the age of 30.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] From age 7 to 12, Spartan boys were taken from their families and placed in military-style barracks for physical and mental training.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Spartan boys were taught to read, write, and do basic math, with a focus on physical toughness and endurance.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Spartan boys were taught to be obedient and disciplined, prioritizing the needs of the state.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] From age 12 to 18, Spartan boys continued with intensive physical exercise and military training, learning to fight with spears, swords, and shields.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] At age 18, boys became full Spartan citizens and were eligible for military service.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] From age 18 to 20, Spartan men served in the military as basic infantry.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] From age 20 to 30, they could serve as hoplite soldiers, requiring more physical fitness and combat training.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Spartan training regimen aimed to produce highly skilled and disciplined soldiers willing to sacrifice for the state.
- [USER] User expressed surprise at the intensity of the Spartan training.
- [USER] User inquired about whether Spartan women received similar training.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Spartan women did not receive military training or participate in physical activities like running or wrestling.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Spartan women received education in reading, writing, and music, which was unusual for women in ancient Greece.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Spartan women enjoyed more freedom and social status than women in other Greek city-states.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Spartan women were encouraged to exercise for health, as healthy women were believed to produce healthy babies.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Spartan women had greater property rights and could own land and inherit wealth.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] While not trained for military combat, Spartan women were expected to be strong, resilient, and independent.
